subject: 5-Bullet Friday — Feel-Good Movies, Fixing Elbow Problems, Reinvention over Stagnation, Fast Thinkers, and More

bullets.section: New movie on my must-watch list
bullets.title: The Peanut Butter Falcon
bullets.note: If you want a hilarious feel-good movie, look no further. I’d never heard of this film, but a great physical therapist and entrepreneur recommended it, and I’m already planning on watching it again. The viewer ratings are incredible ([96% on Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_peanut_butter_falcon)), and, c’mon, how can you not bite after this description? >>> “After running away from a residential nursing home to pursue his dream of becoming a pro wrestler, a man who has Down syndrome befriends an outlaw who becomes his coach and ally.” The fantastic cast includes [Shia LaBeouf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_LaBeouf), [Dakota Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakota_Johnson), and [Zack Gottsagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Gottsagen). Check out the trailer [here](https://youtu.be/UNl9RqjLCwc?si=lcpmFXm7eckFvmw_).

bullets.title: Personal Renewal
bullets.creator: John Gardner, delivered to McKinsey & Company on November 10, 1990
bullets.note:
, delivered to McKinsey & Company on November 10, 1990. One of my favorite paragraphs is this one early on:

_Not long ago, I read a splendid article on barnacles. I don’t want to give the wrong impression of the focus of my reading interests. Sometimes days go by without my reading about barnacles, much less remembering what I read. But this article had an unforgettable opening paragraph. “The barnacle,” the author explained “is confronted with an existential decision about where it’s going to live. Once it decides … it spends the rest of its life with its head cemented to a rock.” End of quote. For a good many of us, it comes to that._

bullets.title: Michael O’Leary, CEO of Ryanair
bullets.note: ([Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/michael-oleary-ceo-of-ryanair/id1614211565?i=1000587206737), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/5hh7CAtWdT8476Bc5oi0vx)) on the _In Good Company_ podcast with [Nicolai Tangen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolai_Tangen). Nicolai is the inimitable CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM), and he has interviewed guests ranging from Jensen Huang to Magnus Carlsen. I’ve been fascinated by O’Leary since I read [_Ryanair: How a Small Irish Airline Conquered Europe_](https://www.amazon.com/Ryanair-Story-Controversial-Low-Cost-Airline/dp/1845132939/ref=sr_1_1?crid=3VMQHKJF9POA7&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.X0hnU0oFjEYUhQrovkbSdloOXntifXIbFvkrahp-OmT6EKUy2wyfHfgD0_htXGp--olnZ_QxqOv8rU5FwNOsfUUmvTXYz-K2ffOOycFDpF9PS9C0FlemSPgXG4SzFbOgeZvD_upStoPHwjUaF4ot8z3YM2MQmZu8GeORGY_a5dzxFrbGXALoJVCncKNuFY5_qhjwfr-to9-YxpLSUbqcfot4x8Fgbrvx6beAbjuFea0.CeMpqmOitj_fr7tbB24I2DJXEG5aWx_X4F_F5BC4Fzc&dib_tag=se&keywords=ryanair&qid=1739564022&s=books&sprefix=ryanair%2Cstripbooks%2C154&sr=1-1) in 2007. The story of Ryanair is truly bonkers, and while O’Leary is controversial, he is brilliant, uncommonly strategic, and unbelievably fast on his feet. Listen to 10–15 minutes of this and you’ll see what I mean.
